title: Honeycomb MCP Server
summary: Query Honeycomb traces, datasets and SLOs from your agent through Honeycomb's hosted MCP server, signed in with OAuth.
description: Honeycomb runs the server itself, which means you install nothing locally. Once connected, an agent can run queries on your event data, fetch a trace, look up column definitions and review SLOs while it works on a slow endpoint or an error spike.

You sign in with OAuth in the browser. The consent screen lets you choose read-only access, so the agent can investigate without creating boards or triggers. Teams in the EU region use the eu1 address instead of the one in this setup.
useWhen: Find what changed when p99 latency doubled
Pull the slowest traces for one endpoint
Check how much error budget an SLO has left
Look up which attributes exist on a dataset before writing a query

mcp.name: honeycomb
access: Reads queries, traces, datasets and SLOs in the Honeycomb environments you authorize
Can create boards, triggers and SLOs only if you grant write access at sign-in

example.prompt: In the checkout dataset, which route had the biggest rise in p99 duration since 13:00, and show one slow trace.
example.result: POST /checkout/confirm: p99 went from 0.9 s to 3.4 s. Slow trace 7f3a...: 2.8 s of the 3.1 s sits in the inventory.reserve span, waiting on a database call.

faq.question: How do I sign in?
faq.answer: Add the URL to your agent and start it. The agent opens a Honeycomb login page and asks which access to grant. Choose read-only for all resources.

faq.question: I am in the EU region. Which URL?
faq.answer: Use https://mcp.eu1.honeycomb.io/mcp in place of the US address.

faq.question: Can I use an API key instead?
faq.answer: Yes, for agents that cannot do an interactive login. Honeycomb documents a management key sent as a bearer token. OAuth is the preferred route.
